report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to add a system-level policy/safety/behavior prompt — i.e., to push the model toward following instructions / safety guidelines (refusing or reframing disallowed/harmful content and producing cautious, policy‑worded responses). In other words: an alignment/safety finetune (a system-prompt-style behaviour injected at generation start).

Why I conclude that
1. The difference is concentrated at the first token position across many layers
   - The L2 norm table shows huge differences at pos0 (the first token) beginning in the mid-to-late layers (layers 4–25) and smaller changes at subsequent token positions. That pattern is exactly what you get when a finetune effectively implants a persistent “system prompt” or initial-behavior vector that changes the model’s generation from the very first token onward (instead of changing some transient downstream feature). It looks like a stable, prompt‑like behavioral bias added to the residual stream at sequence start.

2. The logit-lens top tokens are strongly consistent with policy/instruction/safety language
   - Early-layer top tokens (pos0) include many directive/administrative tokens (“Do”, “Non”, “Check”, “Every”, “Stay”, “Best”, “recommend”, “consider”, “ensure”, “strive”, “optimize”) — these are the kinds of words that steer phrasing toward instructions, checks, and caution.
   - Other high-scoring tokens across layers include words associated with harm/medical/legal contexts (“surgeon”, “clinic”, “law”, “tragedy”, “tragic”, “rescue”, “corpses”, “sorrow”, “wrong”, “rejected”, “damaged”). That mix looks like the model is primed to treat potentially risky inputs as safety-relevant topics (legal/medical/violent/tragic) and to apply guarded language or to refuse/reframe.
   - Tokens at intermediate layers indicating empathy/mitigation (“focus”, “peace”, “Everyone”, “regret”, “relevant”, “restoration”, “donor”, “recommendations”) support the idea the finetune encourages safer or more supportive phrasing rather than raw or harmful content.

3. The progression across layers fits a behavioral/policy injection
   - Early-mid layers show content/style words (e.g., product/venue words like “bottle”, “wings” in very low layers — noise or dataset artifacts), but from layers ~11–25 the top tokens shift to clear policy/instruction/ safety motifs. That matches a learned, persistent instruction signal that influences generation more strongly in later layers where decoding decisions are solidified.

Why other hypotheses are less likely
- It does not look like a narrow domain finetune (e.g., medical-only or product-review-only), because the token set mixes directive/policy words and safety/legal/medical tokens rather than a consistent domain vocabulary.
- It is not simply stylistic (e.g., more verbose or more formal) because the token changes emphasize directive verbs and refusal/mitigation vocabulary rather than purely stylistic markers.

Confidence: high
- The pos0 concentration is a strong structural clue that something like a system prompt or alignment objective was implanted, and the lexicon changes (refusal/safety/instruction words and legal/medical/tragic vocabulary) point toward safety/alignment rather than a topical shift.

Concise summary
- Finetuning objective: implant a system-level alignment/safety policy so the model follows safety guidelines (refuse/reframe disallowed requests, use cautious/mitigating language, and prioritize instruction-style phrasing).
- Evidence: large pos0 residual changes across many layers (system-prompt signature) + logit-lens tokens that cluster around instruction verbs, refusal/mitigation words, and safety/legal/medical/tragic topics.
